criteria.text: Identifies that the MAC carve-outs (general economic, industry-wide and pandemic changes) contain no 'disproportionate effect' exception, so the Buyer bears those risks even where the Company is disproportionately affected, and recommends adding one.
Identifies that the 5-year SPA non-compete may be unenforceable as wider than reasonably necessary and is inconsistent with the 18-month restriction in the Founder's employment agreement.
Calculates the working capital shortfall as $350,000 and the adjusted Purchase Price as $209,650,000, identifying that the Seller's funds flow figure of $209,300,000 is wrong.

Identifies the threatened $3,400,000 claim by Fenwick Robotics Ltd recorded in the board minutes and that it is not disclosed against the litigation warranty (Warranty 7.1), recommending a specific indemnity or price protection.
Identifies that the warranty cap in SPA Section 8.3 is stated as $25,200,000 but 10% of the $210,000,000 Purchase Price is $21,000,000, i.e. the stated figure is wrong.
Explains how 'material adverse effect' could be read narrowly or broadly and what each reading means for the Buyer's walk-away right.
Shows the adjustment arithmetic ($210,000,000 - $350,000 = $209,650,000) and flags the discrepancy.
Shows proposed drafting changes as before/after (current wording vs proposed wording) with a one-line rationale.
